Why Did I Intervene?
This Preface is a personal rendition of an introduction to this professional
engineering testimony. Whereas the report body attempts to present in
third person, this preface is intentionally ﬁrst person.
To start. Others’ words are often better than ours, and when old, others’
words are best. Winston’s Churchill’s words on inaction and
consequences are a notable example.

Fundamentally, Mr. Churchill’s quote is one primary why.I.am.
intervening… to challenge the “conﬁrmed unteachability of mankind.” I
know we can do better. The question is, will we? Or even more
importantly, will we, voluntarily.
I am under no illusion that more than a few will read this testimony, and
perhaps even fewer, this preface. I am under no illusion that this
testimony will “move the needle” to any noticeable degree. The die
seems to have been cast.
It seems similarly likely the PUC Commissioners or authoritative staff will
read it. I have been told by some this entire testimony is a colossal waste
 SECOND SUPPLEMENT TO THE DIRECT TESTIMONY OF THOMAS F. GREEN, P.E. |
       PUC DOCKET NO. 59475; SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349 | Page 3
 of time. If you are reading it, my resulting expectation is you are likely an
advisor on some level, but not a decider. I also imagine also you are
reading not so much as to absorb and consider, but instead to rebut.
This testimony may not matter. It may not be heard. But that doesn’t
mean it should not be said.
Cognitive dissidence is a difficult thing to overcome: that is, receiving and
absorbing new information which is contrary to our biases or
perspectives is a difficult challenge. It is anthropologically imbedded into
us to give highest credibility to what we know from our past experiences.
It’s instinctive. It’s survival. It requires self-training to overcome.
Throughout this testimony, relevant and legitimate questions are being
asked. Perhaps some answers will be tendered in words. But those
answers are but preliminary. The words are not the answers: words are
always drowned out by decisions and actions. So, answers will come
with decisions and actions. Answers will demonstrate priorities, and to
what parties those priorities serve in the highest.
The “Why are you intervening?” question is one I have often asked of
myself. In addition to Mr. Churchill’s inspiration to do better, one of my
“whys” was conveyed back in October 2025 when I submitted to LCRA its
public survey/questionnaire form the Lampasas public meeting.. More
speciﬁcally, my answer to Question No. 12 applies historically to this
continuing question. Excerpting that discussion from Exhibit 1- LCRA
Feedback Questionnaire:


“12. Do you have any general remarks or comments?



 SECOND SUPPLEMENT TO THE DIRECT TESTIMONY OF THOMAS F. GREEN, P.E. |
       PUC DOCKET NO. 59475; SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349 | Page 4
 Yes, quite a few, thank you. All are in full candor, all offered with
respect. I’d say if you, any of “yous,” were in our shoes, you, too,
would have similar comments/questions.
A preface, if I may. Two “Land Men” (those who negotiate the land
seizure and eminent domain issues) have stated a very clear
message (paraphrasing): “They just don’t care, at all, about the
landowners. The Utilities don’t care. The PUC doesn’t care. ERCOT
doesn’t care. They are going to take whatever they want and there’s
nothing you can do about it… nothing at all. Money drives them all.
When it comes to compensation for seized and damaged land, they
pay the minimums because that is better for their inﬂated bottom
lines. The public involvement in the process is political lip service.”
But I have a hard time believing their perspectives are correct in the
great Republic of Texas in which my family has been bred, born and
raised for 7 generations. In fact, I choose to not believe them.
However, their message does beg the question, is this still our
Texas, or does it solidly belong to those who can buy inﬂuence? I
ask the question, how, in fact, in detail, are landowner values and
perspectives analyzed and how do they alter whatever the preferred
position of the PUC and Utilities are? I seek not word salads in
response, but factual, documented, and transparent data. “You” are
unneedfully seizing property, greatly reducing its values, creating
irreparable and signiﬁcant health, environmental and economic
damage. I, we, deserve a FULL accounting and copies of reports and
other evidence of why this approach has been taken, and what
alternatives have been thoroughly analyzed and by whom.



 SECOND SUPPLEMENT TO THE DIRECT TESTIMONY OF THOMAS F. GREEN, P.E. |
       PUC DOCKET NO. 59475; SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349 | Page 5
 Again, the above and below items are direct, but intended with the
utmost respect to you, the people who serve us, the citizens.
Thank you.”
As noted above, I was in disbelief that Texas had become what the land
men shared from their long-standing experience. I now know I could be
naively wrong. My belief above has this far turned out to be a nostalgic
fantasy from my West Texas rural roots. I suppose time will tell.
As evidenced from the above No. 12, I didn’t start out where I am
currently standing. But, by all accounts of what I have discovered since
receiving the ﬁrst LCRA/Oncor “notice,” the land men are right.
I.still.seek?.indeed.battle?.to.prove.them.wrong¡
 All.the.players.are.Executive.Branch¡.The PUC makes the rules, the
SOAH administers the rules in a quasi-judicial form, and then the PUC
makes all the ﬁnal judgments. It decides: accept, deny, or change
however it duly elects. Historically, those judgments and decisions seem
to consistently favor the industries (e.g., transmission companies) which
the PUC is supposed to regulate… for the protection of Texans. From the
public’s perspective, the system is woefully awry.
So, once again, back to the question… why intervene. There are reasons I
and most of the rest are compelled to do so. The Exhibit 2 My Why
(Intervene), gives my personal fuller picture. The following excerpt
captures the essence from a history of life lessons:
  • “Do the right thing.
  • Never be a quitter.
  • Help neighbors near and far. Do not fight them.
  • Apply my professional duties.
 SECOND SUPPLEMENT TO THE DIRECT TESTIMONY OF THOMAS F. GREEN, P.E. |
       PUC DOCKET NO. 59475; SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349 | Page 6
   • Battle for a win-win.


I have sought and continue to seek to do the right thing and to give good
cause, to implore and to inspire others to do so. My January 2026 letter
to Governor Abbott (Exhibit 3) conveys that message. It also conveys
that the right thing is to Pause and Re-evaluate, a step that can be
expeditiously achieved as presented in my subsequently downgraded
testimony in Dockets 59029 and 59182. The closing paragraph of that
letter to our Governor reads:
»Everybody.knows.something• .nobody.knows.everything• .about.
anything¡.Bringing.a.proper.team.with.divergent.experiences.together.to.
rapidly.converge.on.solutions.for.the.host.of.unprecedented.issues.is.
both.logical.and.responsible.to.Texans¡.It is the right thing to do.”


The unfortunate battle.
I do not come to this testimony either voluntarily or as an adversary to
any party. I come because I have been thrust into a battle in which the
law a PE serves compels him to engage… despite the near zero
resources now available, especially after the ﬂood. I recognize the
unfortunate reality that the “system” pits parties in opposition. There are
much better and more productive approaches than excluding the public
in the planning and later involving the public in only a last step façade in
which it hopes it will dissuade the already vested planners. If the process
is ﬂawed, the results are as well.
Accordingly, with battle lines drawn, my life and professional value of
“win-win” will not be easy. For the CCN applicant, its position is a must
 SECOND SUPPLEMENT TO THE DIRECT TESTIMONY OF THOMAS F. GREEN, P.E. |
       PUC DOCKET NO. 59475; SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349 | Page 7
 “win” for its shareholders, at all costs and by whatever methods it needs
to employ. For the Professional Engineer, it is not about a “win,” but
instead about a truthful advocacy for the public.
It is so very unfortunate that the applicants may not be true or right, but
win anyway because of their.incumbency.and.well‗honed massive.
ﬁnancial.and.personnel.resources far, far beyond those of the intervenor
or even the collection of intervenors. Though the individual intervenor nor
the collection of intervenors has not even a morsel of the applicant’s
resources, the Professional.Engineer.nonetheless.has.a..duty.to.the.
public.different.than.any.of.the.other.parties?.and.therefore.necessarily.
seeks.to.take.whatever.action.is.needed.to.comply.with.its.duty• .all the
while under the severely limited resources and available time.
Doing anything otherwise would not just be complacent, it would be
complicit. And with legitimate public issues surrounding the PBRP and
the ensuing CCNs, a complicit acceptance of the issues would not only
be wrong morally, it would be professionally suspect.
The PE’s role is not about winning. It is about doing.the.right.thing by
Texans.
Contrary to having a career of constantly seeing and working on solving
complex problems, though not without challenge, I remain a self-
professed optimist. I must hold to the ethical foundation that people will
do the right thing, again noting that the right thing has zero affiliation with
where money lands.
A glimpse into this testimony report.
Given this partial background, this report is authored with the intent to
include, but not necessarily be limited to, the following topics: questions,

 SECOND SUPPLEMENT TO THE DIRECT TESTIMONY OF THOMAS F. GREEN, P.E. |
       PUC DOCKET NO. 59475; SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349 | Page 8
 information, ﬁndings, conclusions, and/or recommendations regarding
the Permian Basin Reliability Plan and therefore the respective Import
Path 2 CCNs. By doing so, it also addresses the other Import Paths. This
report includes background or history in some cases, but it is
fundamentally intended to be forward thinking.
Preface Closing:
So… within the report, there will be statements or questions or critiques
or scrutiny regarding the appropriateness of certain elements of the Plan
and its Import Path 2 CCN(s). Such critiques are not intended to unduly
criticize any party’s character, and no disparagement is intended. The
critiques are simply the obligation of being forthright.
This report testimony is authored by the cited Professional Engineer,
Thomas F. Green. Within the report are both technical/engineering
discussions and questions, and conclusions reached to date. True to the
Professional Engineering ethics, the questions, discussions, and
conclusions are presented forthrightly and are truthful to the best of the
author’s knowledge.
I am in no way, form, or fashion intending to “poke the bear.” I in fact
welcome the presumed rebuttal to this testimony.
I fully recognize there will be debate, some likely spirited, regarding
elements of this report. I welcome such, not as a contest of wit or will, or.
even.winning, but instead as a primary objective to serve Texans the best
they can be served. It is an objective that may not be easily achieved, but
it IS an objective that is… still… achievable.
The ultimate question:


 SECOND SUPPLEMENT TO THE DIRECT TESTIMONY OF THOMAS F. GREEN, P.E. |
       PUC DOCKET NO. 59475; SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349 | Page 9
 The question is whether or not the primary objective to do the right thing
will be achieved, given the monumental disparity of resources of the
applicants compared to the intervenors, and given the ongoing and
lasting relations between the applicants and the PUC.
We will see what the parties’ priorities are by the decisions made.
Respectfully submitted,




Tom Green, P.E.
A work in progress: Mr. Green does not and cannot testify that this report
is perfect. Indeed, given the impossible scope and timing required of this
testimony, it is not a polished document. It has rough edges. It’s not the
author’s best work, but it the best that it could do under the
circumstances. All parties must acknowledge, as with any exploratory
effort such as this one, it is a work in progress. The author may, at its
discretion, amend or supplement the report testimony verbally or in
writing as more information is learned.

                             End of Preface




 SECOND SUPPLEMENT TO THE DIRECT TESTIMONY OF THOMAS F. GREEN, P.E. |
       PUC DOCKET NO. 59475; SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349 | Page 10
